title: Non-Hermitian-enhanced quantum sensing in an optical interferometer
authors: X. J. Huang, Lei Xiao, Bingzi Huo, X. X. Yi, Peng Xue
abstract: The precision of quantum parameter estimation is traditionally constrained by the quantum Cramér-Rao bound, which is based on the Hermitian measurement framework. Recent studies of non-Hermitian systems have suggested new possibilities for enhancing parameter-estimation sensitivity. Here, we experimentally realize quantum parameter estimation using a non-Hermitian observable on a linear optical platform. The parameter is encoded in single-photon probe states and read out with a Sagnac interferometer, which allows us to reconstruct the complex expectation value of the implemented non-Hermitian observable from interference fringes. We observe a reduced error-propagation variance compared with the optimal Hermitian observable for the same probe-state model. This advantage remains visible under amplitude-damping noise. We further analyze the complete optical measurement as a physical positive-operator-valued measure (POVM) and show, through the corresponding classical Fisher information (CFI), that the observed non-Hermitian advantage is consistent with the standard quantum metrological limit when all output ports are included. Our results provide an experimental route to non-Hermitian observable readout and clarify its operational meaning in quantum sensing.
summary: The paper experimentally demonstrates enhanced quantum parameter estimation sensitivity by employing a non-Hermitian observable readout technique on an optical interferometer. Using single photons in a Sagnac setup, the authors show that the resulting error variance is lower than the best Hermitian counterpart, even with noise present. This work provides a practical route for implementing and validating non-Hermitian concepts in quantum sensing.
main_problem: The primary goal is to enhance quantum parameter estimation sensitivity beyond limits set by standard Hermitian measurements by utilizing non-Hermitian observables.
main_result: The experiment successfully demonstrated a reduced error-propagation variance using a non-Hermitian observable compared to the optimal Hermitian one, an advantage that persists under amplitude-damping noise.
method: Quantum parameter estimation was performed experimentally using a single-photon Sagnac interferometer setup. The non-Hermitian expectation value was reconstructed by analyzing interference fringes from multiple output ports.
model_or_system: The physical platform is a linear optical system utilizing single-photon probe states and a Sagnac interferometer. Non-Hermiticity is implemented through controllable, polarization-dependent photon loss within the measurement path.

paper_structure: The paper details the theoretical framework of using non-Hermitian Fisher information, describes the experimental setup involving SPDC and the Sagnac interferometer for readout, presents measurements showing variance reduction with non-Hermitian observables, and concludes by confirming consistency with standard quantum limits via POVM analysis.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete experimental realization of using non-Hermitian physics in metrology. It is highly relevant to open quantum systems and quantum optics as it shows how engineered dissipation (non-Hermiticity) can enhance sensing while remaining physically consistent when measured fully.
